A process_only verifier (every browser/PWA) may credit wall-clock gaps between runtime segments only under its Recommended profile, only forward of a durable wall high-water mark, and only with a final authenticated veto sweep before accepting; Hardened/Maximum verifiers remain monotonic-only (ADR-0154).

The validity of an object carrying an extension registered as non-critical never depends on the registry version a client ships: with the wire critical bit false, a wrong owning object, non-map payload, unknown/missing field or registered bound violation makes the extension unusable (ignored, bytes preserved) and the object stays valid; a wire-criticality mismatch rejects the object; critical registrations keep reject-on-malformed. V1 presentation extensions bind only to the RichText they were validated against and never carry across message.edit (ADR-0155).

Offline-local LAN delivery follows ADR-0157 LanDeliveryProfile-v1: 15-minute HMAC rendezvous epochs with fresh link_nonce and K=8 fixed-cardinality advertisements; TLS 1.3 channel proof bound to the RFC 8446 exporter before identity-bearing objects; ephemeral om-lan-v1 RelayEntry plus fresh route-bound SealedDeliveryKeyRecord; ordinary SealedDeliveryEnvelope for established 1:1, MLS PrivateMessage for groups; MessageRequest/IntroGate for offline first contact; distinct-pool AsyncKeyBundle serving after acceptance; pull/range encrypted-blob transfer; and no weaker browser-only path. LAN reachability never grants identity, relationship, device or group authority.

No engineering scope is authorized until every wire object, event body and extension it introduces has frozen CDDL, registered numeric fields and domain-separation labels, and positive/negative vectors on which two independently written codecs agree; logical JSON schemas never substitute (ADR-0156, ADR-0139).

Scheduled send is a device-local, profile-bound queue: at actual send time the item becomes an ordinary message.create whose EventClock, sending epoch, authorization and expiry are taken then (never backdated); an overdue item is sent at the next opportunity and marked sent-late to the sender; loss of device/profile/membership/relationship eligibility discards it with a local notice and it never migrates to another device (ADR-0156).

Account-private sync records, including implementation-private same-account AccountHistorySnapshot records, carry an implementation/codec identifier bound inside authenticated E2EE framing; an unrecognized record is ignored whole and never partially interpreted. Cross-implementation draft/preference/same-account-history sync is not a V1 interoperability promise. This rule does not apply to the interoperable Room HistoryBundle (ADR-0157 amending ADR-0156).

Every new critical key-23 extension registered after the W0 registry freeze uses an ID beginning with '!'; any OM-CBOR-v1 decoder rejects an unknown '!' ID even when ExtEntry.critical is false; '!' IDs can never be registered non-critical; om.acs.fork_ack and om.acs.legacy_policy are the only grandfathered critical IDs outside that class (ADR-0157).

Room HistoryBundle is an interoperable groups-scope protocol object, not implementation-private device sync. Before groups authorization V-004 freezes its wire schema/fields/labels and two-codec vectors; newcomer rendering attributes bundled history to the bundle author and retains the existing expiry/delete/redaction exclusions and cooperative history_policy semantics (ADR-0157).

A PWA/browser claims local_delivery only when its PlatformAdapter provides a direct-local transport with channel binding equivalent to ADR-0157's TLS-exporter proof; otherwise it reports local_delivery unavailable and does not use weaker browser-specific identity or sender-hiding semantics.

permanently_revoked_devices is a monotone DeviceID tombstone set: a revoked DeviceID can never re-enter active_control_devices or messaging_devices in a descendant ACS; returning/recovered hardware uses a fresh DeviceID and fresh DeviceCredential, while old credential material may remain only for historical signature verification (ADR-0161).

RelaySet and BlobLocationRecord hash chains use exact +1 parent continuity, retain concurrent valid branches/out-of-order children as continuity knowledge, and select the effective currently-eligible record deterministically by highest version then lexicographically smallest canonical record hash; arrival order, version jumps and cross-lineage previous hashes cannot choose protocol state (ADR-0161).

Room HistoryBundle is bound to ConversationID, author device/account, recipient account plus immutable membership incarnation, and a GroupControlState/MLS epoch where both are admitted; bundle-local history items are inert archive/display data whose claimed EventIDs/authors never enter live ConversationEvent dedupe or execute any Room/control reducer (ADR-0161).

AccountControlState.minimum_crypto_profile is the account-wide 1:1 minimum only: it must reference a profile with security_generation.one_to_one; ordinary ACS replacement is a raise only when that value strictly increases, profile ids and group generations never order it, and Room/group floors independently use security_generation.group (ADR-0161).

The reference-client default shell is conversation-first: conversations/current conversation plus Omnibar/new-conversation/profile are persistent; Calls and People remain first-class/contextually reachable and optionally pinnable but are not mandatory permanent navigation destinations (ADR-0162).

Omnibar adaptive ranking is IdentityProfile-local/account-private presentation state; it may use pins, match quality, successful-selection frequency/recency and local context but does not require durable raw query history, never pools profiles, and does not contact external discovery merely on local focus/typing (ADR-0162).

Omnibar rank/popularity is never identity confidence or protocol authority; destructive/recovery/control/provider/permission/plaintext-egress suggestions retain ordinary typed Core intent and confirmation/authorization, and asynchronous result arrival cannot silently replace the keyboard-armed target before activation (ADR-0162).

OM UI uses semantic color/icon roles with non-color-only state; untrusted themes cannot reassign status/security meaning or replace semantic action/security glyphs, and built-in light/dark themes pass accessibility/contrast validation (ADR-0162).

Theme import rejects absolute/traversal/backslash-alias/NUL/duplicate-normalized asset paths before extraction, verifies declared hashes/lengths, uses bounded streamed sandbox extraction and applies atomically; no conforming theme importer has an unbounded extraction path (ADR-0162).

Density, explicit motion intensity/reduced-motion and notification/call alert policy are user/accessibility/platform settings that outrank theme defaults; themes may style spacing/easing/sounds only inside those bounds and cannot silence/re-enable alert policy (ADR-0162).

Shared call UI preserves an explicitly user-pinned participant/video tile across active-speaker changes, keeps pin controls keyboard/screen-reader operable and avoids covering the primary face/hands region with captions/controls where layout permits (ADR-0162).

A durable mutating operation that can cross a crash/network uncertainty boundary persists its existing stable logical identity plus security-relevant parent/context before the first externally visible effect where required; timeout after possible transmission is an unknown outcome, exact retry reuses the same logical/idempotency identity, and a second semantic mutation is not created merely because an acknowledgement was lost (ADR-0163).

Group membership/role transitions use a crash-safe local journal: intent and exact Commit/Binding are durable before publication; relay ack is not canonical acceptance; tentative MLS/application state cannot send messages or become canonical; accepted MLS state + GroupControlState/head/dedupe promote atomically or via equivalent recovery journal; losing/stale candidates are inert/superseded and long-offline restart reconciles first (ADR-0163).

Core exposes provider-neutral Committed/PendingAuthorization/PendingNetwork/PendingReconciliation/NeedsUserAction/Rejected outcomes; a possible lost-response mutation is pending/reconciling rather than terminal rejection, stale/conflict refreshes authenticated state before a new semantic mutation, and UI restart does not originate a duplicate action from missing acknowledgement (ADR-0163).

Every engineering scope has a machine-readable implementation-readiness contract whose authorization dependencies exactly match repository_contract.json, whose normative sources exist, and which declares restart/retry/forbidden-shortcut rules; integration prerequisites never become hidden authorization or protocol-authority dependencies (ADR-0163).

Every dangerous algorithm listed by ADR-0164 has a machine-readable contract naming normative sources, states, verification boundary and forbidden shortcuts; the contract does not replace those sources or authorize engineering.

AccountControlState child validation derives all deltas from the authenticated parent, validates authorization/monotonicity/revocation/profile-floor constraints before acceptance, and never substitutes generation magnitude, arrival order or group crypto generation for authority.

1:1 inbound and sealed-delivery acceptance performs bounded outer validation, durable RESERVED replay state, authenticated RelationshipContext/ACS/device eligibility and session checks before plaintext/application release; exact retries remain idempotent and stale-head uncertainty is reconciled rather than treated as definitive rejection.

Group Commit implementation follows the durable INTENT_DURABLE -> CANDIDATE_PREPARED -> PUBLISHED_UNCONFIRMED -> ACCEPTED journal, preserves exact prepared Commit bytes, isolates tentative state, and reconciles canonical state before promotion after restart or concurrency.

Mutable route/location branches, Room HistoryBundle imports, protocol extensions, LAN frames and unknown provider outcomes use the ADR-0164 ordering/failure algorithms: no arrival-order authority, live-history reducer injection, criticality downgrade, pre-proof identity exposure, plaintext fallback or timeout-as-rejection.

Published registry/profile identifiers, frozen W0 object shapes, domain-separation labels and published (extension_id, version) registrations retain their historical meaning; behavior-changing corrections use a new immutable profile/extension/object lineage or explicit fork rather than mutating the old definition.

Protocol/profile selection for a conversation type uses the validated mutual profile intersection, local policy/lifecycle eligibility and the applicable security floor; the highest security_generation for that conversation type wins, deprecated candidates are avoided for new traffic when an equal-or-higher non-deprecated candidate exists, and equal-generation ties use the smallest profile ID only as a deterministic tie-break. Profile IDs are never security ordering.

A published extension (extension_id, version) tuple is immutable and criticality is immutable for an extension ID; future critical semantics use the ! extension-ID class, while a new version under an existing non-critical ID is permitted only for backward-compatible fallback-safe semantics. Authority/security/ownership/fallback changes require a new extension ID and/or CryptoProfile.

Every normative change is classified into the ADR-0165 change classes, and the class determines required ADR, registry/schema, conformance-vector, migration/reinitialization, threat/requirement traceability and continuity artifacts. Agents must use the strongest applicable class and may not downgrade it for implementation convenience.

A compatible profile migration preserves stable identity and authenticates the transition, advances the applicable security floor, moves new traffic only after new-profile state is established, drains old state within its bounded compatibility window and never silently returns to a profile below the established floor.

Engineering agents must not use highest-version/highest-profile-ID ordering as a security rule, mutate a published CryptoProfile or extension criticality in place, expand frozen W0 wire through logical JSON schemas, treat live registries/project websites as protocol authority, or claim local evolution harnesses as independent/formal/interoperability evidence.
